summary.headline: Ola Electric Q2 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 421 crore with gross margin steady near 30%, as management says demand now exceeds supply.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 421 crore versus Rs 455 crore in Q1, with gross margin of Rs 126 crore (about 30%) versus Rs 139 crore (30.5%). Operating expenses were Rs 369 crore, or about Rs 390 crore after adding back a one-time Rs 57 crore credit in Q1. Operating cash flow improved to negative Rs 188 crore from negative Rs 215 crore, and consolidated debt fell from Rs 3,132 crore (Dec 2024) to Rs 1,800 crore (Sep 2026). Management said the company moved its D2C stores to a dealership model, with 255 dealer partners and 319 stores as of 8 November, and that the constraint is now supply rather than demand.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 330 crore reported in Q1; about Rs 390 crore in Q1 excluding Rs 57 crore one-time credit
vs negative Rs 195 crore in Q1
vs loss of Rs 336 crore in Q1
vs negative Rs 215 crore in Q1
about 45,000 paid-order vehicles slipped into October due to charger shortage

segments.name: Auto (EV scooters, D2C to dealer)
segments.commentary: Dealer count reached 255 partners and 319 stores by 8 November, with a target of 450 stores by December and about 700+ by March 2027. Channel inventory is about 15 days, and management says the company is moving to a dealer model with negative working capital.

segments.name: Cell (gigafactory)
segments.commentary: Commissioned 6 GWh capacity (3.5 GW added) with COD on 23 September. NMC yields are in the mid-70s% with a target of mid-80s over the next couple of months; the target is 90%. PLI benefits are expected from next quarter, and the ACC PLI has been extended to 2031.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected to fall to about 4% as dealer commissions are deducted, while operating margin is expected to improve to about 3% and beyond.
Company stores to close by December, with opex falling further as the store network shuts; management expects the auto business to reach near- to mid-term free cash flow.
Cell business: NMC integration into own auto products from next quarter, with own LFP cell production towards the end of FY27 or early Q1; 30% of auto volumes to use NMC and 70% LFP.
FY28 planning assumption of about 5 kWh average pack per vehicle, so 2-3 GWh of cell output implies roughly 400-500k vehicles.

Cell capacity to go from 6 GWh to 20 GWh over the mid-to-long term after stabilising 6 GWh over the next couple of quarters; capex per GWh expected below Rs 400 crore at 20 GWh, to be funded partly by external equity in the cell company.
Gen 3/4 product with 4680 cells is targeted for Q4, with launch timing dependent on demand and supply.
capex_capacity: Cell gigafactory commissioned at 6 GWh (3.5 GW added), COD 23 September 2026; described as the only gigafactory at this scale commissioned in India.
Cell utilisation to ramp step by step as NMC and LFP cells are integrated into own products first, then into energy storage.
Capex to scale from 6 GWh to 20 GWh is expected to be much smaller than the 0-6 GWh build; the factory is designed for 20 GWh.
Delivery of the 4680-based vehicle is targeted for Q4 FY27, with the launch date subject to testing and demand.
Rs 5,000 crore IPO plus Rs 2,500 crore pre-IPO equity, plus QIP and rights issue; rights issue 60% paid, with 40% call date not yet announced.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds supply: about 5,000 paid-order vehicles had deliveries pushed by a week into October due to charger unavailability.
Management said about 45,000 vehicles were ready but could not be booked as revenue in Q2 because chargers were not available.
Gross margin decline was mainly from commodity costs, partly offset by a price increase.
Dealer-channel early markets show market share above pre-transition levels, per management; dealer re-ordering is ramping.
Management says its bill of materials is 15-20% below competitors (around Rs 80-85k per vehicle), attributed to in-house engineering and vertical integration.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q2 vehicle volumes, and is the QoQ gross margin dip due to commodities or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were about 35,000-36,000 booked; about 45,000 paid vehicles slipped to October. The margin dip was mainly commodity-driven, with a partial price increase offsetting part of it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery pack size used to derive FY28 unit volumes from 2-3 GWh of cell output?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to plan on about 5 kWh per vehicle for FY28, versus about 3.8 kWh today, implying roughly 400-500k vehicles from 2-3 GWh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dealer commission and its effect on the auto margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the introductory dealer commission will fall over the next two to three quarters, and gross margin will decline but operating margin will rise. It declined to confirm the Rs 11,000 per-vehicle estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in the ramp from mid-70s% yields to 90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields are already in the mid-70s% for NMC with a clear roadmap to mid-80s over the next couple of months and 90% later. It said the cell business has been in development since 2020.

qa_highlights.question: How will GST refunds affect cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30-40% of the receivable is inverted duty structure and the rest will be consumed in future business. Approval timelines are expected to fall from 3-4 months to 1-2 months from 1 November.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 4680 product be delivered on time, and what is the cost advantage of in-house cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product is targeted for Q4 and launch timing depends on demand. The in-house cell is expected to deliver about a 20% cost advantage over 2170 cells at scale.

risks_watch: Supply and component constraints (chargers, supplier ramp-up) are holding back deliveries; the paid order backlog must be cleared.
Dealer margin structure is introductory and could change; gross margin is guided lower.
NMC yield ramp from mid-70s% toward 90%, plus PLI receipt timing and the cell business's dependence on external equity for the 20 GWh expansion.
Working capital and GST refund timing; about 30-40% of the receivable is tied to inverted duty and may not convert to cash quickly.
The rights issue balance (40% unpaid) and the call date are unannounced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, dealer ramp and cell commissioning, with numbers offered in a hedged manner on yields and timelines. Management avoided precise figures on share count and equity raised, and gave a loose answer on the 4680 product launch timing.
key_quotes: If there is one headline for Q2 or even going forward, it is demand is no longer our constraint.
Demand is ahead of supply and we can sell every vehicle we produce.
So overall demand is no longer a constraint.

growth.why: Management guides dealer stores to ~700+ by March 2027 and cell capacity to scale 6 to 20 GWh over the mid-to-long term, with 6 GWh commissioned 23 Sep; but Q2 revenue fell to Rs 421 cr from Rs 455 cr, EBITDA loss widened to Rs 246 cr, and no revenue growth % is guided, so outlook is flat with partial backing (charger constraint and ~45,000 unbooked vehicles are the gating items).

rows.when: Q2 FY27 (done); 450 stores by Dec, ~700+ by Mar 2027
rows.why: 6 GWh cell gigafactory commissioned with COD on 23 Sep 2026 (3.5 GW added), and dealer stores reached 319 on 8 Nov with targets of 450 by December and about 700+ by March 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: About 45,000 paid-order vehicles slipped into October due to charger shortage, and management says demand exceeds supply, but Q2 revenue fell to Rs 421 cr from Rs 455 cr and volumes were about 35,000-36,000 booked.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on demand and dealer re-ordering, with a 45,000-vehicle backlog, but no revenue growth % is guided and supply constraints gate conversion.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin guided down toward about 4%, NMC yields in mid-70s% against a 90% target, and GST refund and rights-issue timing are unresolved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gen 3/4 vehicle with 4680 cells targeted for Q4, but launch timing is explicitly dependent on demand and supply, and management gave a loose answer on timing.

rows.label: Company stores close by December; opex falls further
rows.why: Company-owned D2C stores are to close by December as the dealer model takes over; Q2 opex was Rs 369 cr versus about Rs 390 cr in Q1 excluding the one-time credit.

rows.label: Consolidated debt down to Rs 1,800 cr
rows.why: Consolidated debt fell from Rs 3,132 cr in Dec 2024 to Rs 1,800 cr in Sep 2026, though operating cash flow remained negative at Rs 188 cr in Q2.

rows.label: GST refund approvals speed up
rows.why: Approval timelines are expected to fall from 3-4 months to 1-2 months, but about 30-40% of the receivable is inverted duty and may not convert to cash quickly.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand exceeding supply, the dealer ramp and cell commissioning, but hedged on NMC yield timing, 4680 launch timing and the rights-issue call date; analysts pushed on the dealer commission and its margin effect, yield ramp and GST refund cash timing.
